title: Remapping Shortcuts can't display its window when powershell is already running.

status.label: Clarify PowerShell activation behavior
status.detail: The report says Alt+Q does not bring up PowerShell when an instance already exists, but lists PowerToys 0.88.0 and does not specify the configured target or current behavior.

judgment.rationale: The report says Alt+Q is used to invoke PowerShell, but it does not identify the exact target configured in Keyboard Manager or whether the expected behavior is to focus an existing window or launch another process. It lists PowerToys 0.88.0. A commenter separately reports that a PowerShell launched through a remap may not receive refreshed system variables until PowerToys is restarted; that does not clarify the reported window-activation failure. A current retest and exact target are needed before assigning a code path.
evidence: The issue lists PowerToys 0.88.0 and says Alt+Q is used to invoke PowerShell.
The author says the remap does not evoke PowerShell when one already exists, while a new launch works.
A commenter reports a separate symptom where a remapped PowerShell process does not refresh system variables until PowerToys is restarted.
The issue has one comment, no assignees, and no current-version reproduction.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the exact Keyboard Manager target and a current-stable retest that distinguishes focusing the existing PowerShell window from starting another process.

fix_assessment.rationale: The old report does not establish whether the remap is expected to activate an existing PowerShell window or launch a new process, and the target configuration is unspecified. A current, precise reproduction is needed before a PowerToys fix can be justified.

issue_context.summary: Alt+Q reportedly fails to bring up PowerShell when a PowerShell instance already exists, but the exact mapping target and activation expectation are unspecified.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.88.0 from GitHub and says it runs as administrator.
The author uses Alt+Q to invoke PowerShell and says an existing instance is not evoked.
The author says launching a new instance works.
A commenter separately reports that environment variables in a remapped PowerShell process may remain stale until PowerToys is restarted.
inferences: The failure may involve the configured launch target or existing-window activation policy rather than shortcut recognition itself.
issue_context.analysis: The report describes a useful symptom, but the actual action configured for Alt+Q and the expected handling of an already-running window are not stated. Ask for those details and a current-stable retest; do not conflate the separate environment-variable comment with the activation issue.
initial_investigation: Read the current issue body and only comment; there are no assignees or linked fixes.
Confirmed the body lists PowerToys 0.88.0 and leaves the exact remap target and expected existing-window behavior unspecified.

information_gaps.information: The exact Keyboard Manager action assigned to Alt+Q and whether the existing-window activation failure still occurs on current stable
information_gaps.why_needed: The target action determines whether the symptom belongs to shortcut delivery, application launch, or existing-window activation.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On current stable, record the configured Alt+Q action, start a PowerShell window, press Alt+Q again, and report whether it focuses that window or launches another instance.

actions.label: Retest PowerShell activation on current stable
